scenario.symptoms: Posting for a user with 80M followers timed out after 30 s. Fan-out worker queue depth hit 2M jobs and normal users’ feeds lagged 45 minutes behind.
scenario.interviewerSetup: The design fan-outs on write synchronously before acknowledging the post API. Celebrity accounts use the same push path as everyone else.

incident.headline: Synchronous fan-out for a celebrity post floods the worker queue

agenda.goal: Distribute posts without blocking writers or starving normal users.
agenda.opener: One celebrity post backed up feeds for everyone—what fan-out strategy would you use instead?

evidence.strong: Hybrid fan-out: push for normal accounts, pull/merge at read for celebrities, async queue with priority tiers.
evidence.adequate: Async queue for all fan-out but still attempts full push for celebrities.
evidence.weak: Synchronous push to all followers before POST returns 200.

misconceptions.pattern: Waiting to finish fan-out before responding to the poster.
misconceptions.challenge: At one millisecond per follower, how long is the HTTP request for 80M followers?

probes: How does a follower’s read path fetch a celebrity post that was not pushed?
Where do you store the list of high-follower accounts?
hints: Fan-out on write vs read is a classic tradeoff.
Celebrities are a tiny fraction of users but most of the fan-out cost.
agenda.referenceFix: Acknowledge posts immediately, async fan-out for normal users, treat mega-influencers as pull-at-read merged with cached timelines, and isolate celebrity jobs into a low-priority queue shard.

nuggets.title: Deleted posts still appear in feeds

scenario.symptoms: Moderation removed a harmful post, but millions of precomputed feeds still show it 12 hours later. Mobile pull-to-refresh intermittently surfaces the deleted content from edge cache.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Feed caches store denormalized post bodies. Deletes update the post service DB but do not invalidate fan-out copies or CDN keys.

incident.headline: Tombstone delete never reaches precomputed feed caches

agenda.goal: Propagate deletes/takedowns to all feed materializations quickly.
agenda.opener: Moderation deleted a post but feeds still show it—how do you fix deletion in this architecture?

evidence.strong: Store post IDs in feeds with hydration, broadcast delete events to trim IDs, purge CDN keys, and filter tombstones on read path.
evidence.weak: Only deletes row in post DB assuming feeds self-heal.

misconceptions.pattern: Believing deleting the canonical row instantly hides content everywhere.
misconceptions.challenge: Where else was the full post body copied?

probes: How do you remove one post ID from millions of feed caches?
What happens if invalidation events are delayed?
hints: Reference feeds by ID to limit blast radius.
Event bus fan-out can carry delete/tombstone messages.
agenda.referenceFix: Emit delete events, strip post IDs from feed caches asynchronously, purge hydration/CDN entries, and enforce tombstone filtering on every read until propagation completes.

nuggets.title: Feed cache stores full posts and OOMs

scenario.symptoms: Redis memory usage climbed 3x after enabling rich media previews in feeds. Editing one viral post required scanning millions of feed keys to patch embedded JSON blobs.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Each follower feed cache entry stores the entire post object. Post edits fan out to every copy.

incident.headline: Denormalized post bodies in every feed explode memory and edit cost

agenda.goal: Keep feed caches small and make post updates cheap.
agenda.opener: Redis ran out of memory after rich media—what should each user’s feed cache actually store?

evidence.strong: Caches ordered post IDs only, hydrates from post cache/DB, handles missing posts gracefully, and localizes edits to post cache.
evidence.adequate: Stores IDs but still embeds large media metadata in feed entries.
evidence.weak: Stores full post JSON per follower feed.

misconceptions.pattern: Duplicating full post bodies into every follower feed.
misconceptions.challenge: How do you update or delete one field on a post copied millions of times?

probes: Walk me through read path latency with ID-only feeds.
How do you batch-hydrate 50 post IDs per request?
hints: Separate timeline structure from content payload.
MGET on a post cache is cheaper than giant feed values.
agenda.referenceFix: Store post IDs (and rank metadata) in feed caches, hydrate via post cache with batch fetch, and invalidate only post cache keys on edit/delete.
